findings.where: the five module glance cards - DATES (x 366-1073, y 310-495), TO DO, DATES THAT MATTER, RITUALS, THE SHELF
findings.what: These cards are machine-cut rectangles with a flat fill and a cast shadow: the flattest 80 px window inside the DATES card measures std 1.47 at (960,400) and the whole TO DO card interior has median 7.50, while the torn rows immediately above and below on the same screen measure 26.1, 42.0 and 51.1 at their flattest and 50-58 median; their left edge holds to a column std of 0.84 px over 155 rows against 2.17 px and a 109 px span on the torn note in 02_chat, corners are dead square, and the wood to the right of the card drops from ~102 to 57 grey levels and recovers over ~15 px.
findings.why: flat.json's own reference says the flattest real 80 px window over a full screen of paper reads 4.58 and the median 33.6, so these cards sit a factor of three under the material's own floor and read as a card widget rather than as stock - the direction the fourth anti-goal warns about, although a 6x contrast stretch of that flattest window (total range 217-231, 13 grey levels) still shows irregular fibre mottle, so it has not arrived at the forbidden object.

findings.where: the header fields strings_read, literals_in_lib, share_of_literals_read and what_it_cannot_see
findings.what: The eight voice rules return zero findings, but they were run over 116 of 3672 literals in lib - 3.2 per cent - and the log names three categories it cannot see at all: a sentence a function returns, a string built by interpolation at the point of use, and anything a module composes from the registry.
findings.why: The product-marketing anti-goal is a claim about every string the app displays, and the evidence certifies it over 3.2 per cent of the literals plus whatever is legible in fifteen artifacts; nothing in evidence closes the other 96.8 per cent.

findings.where: absent, with 16_setup_android.png, per MANIFEST.json missing and WHY_MISSING.json
findings.what: The two Android artifacts are not in the set, so no Android string, no Android notification and no Android rendering of the paper is examined anywhere - all four anti-goals are checked against the PWA under WebKit only.
findings.why: The reason given is a measured standing fact about the machine, not an excuse (no /dev/kvm so the x86_64 image runs under QEMU instruction emulation, adbd answered at 113 minutes with no framework behind it, no GTK for a desktop stand-in, and nothing faked from the PWA), but the consequence for this row is the same: half the shipped surface named in the goal is unexamined for engagement machinery, emoji, voice and paper.

findings.where: the max_ratio field against surfaces.desk.ratio and surfaces.desk_dusk.ratio, and the ok field
findings.what: The log declares max_ratio 3.6 with the rationale that a board with only rings on it is a comb, then measures across-the-grain to along-the-grain ratios of 5.13 (desk.png) and 5.49 (desk_dusk.png) - both over its own threshold - and reports ok: true, the verdict apparently keyed only on least_fine_detail 1.83 clearing min_fine 1.6.
findings.why: A material log that certifies itself against a threshold it fails is the log a reader would lean on when asking whether a surface is a real texture or an approximation, and this one says pass where its own number says comb.

what_is_working: No engagement machinery anywhere I could measure. The tab strip in 01_pulse, 02_chat and 13_messenger_states carries five stamped paper tabs and no badge, count or dot; reception.json's four delivered notifications are titled with the sender's name and bodied 'wrote something', 'said how they are', 'is holding something out' with no count; ritual_kept and read_marker default to 'off' in the notification prefs; 03_us.report.json's rituals glance is 'last: tuesday soup' and the on-screen ritual row reads 'sunday 9 call - 20 times', a plain tally with no best run, no comparison and no warning, which is the 'rituals and streaks' the goal asks for rather than the streak-breakage the anti-goal forbids. My own grep for unlock|earn|reward|achievement|badge|level up|points|streak|keep it up|days in a row|don't break across every file in evidence/logs and every top-level json returns hits only inside strings.json's own rule list.

No emoji and no stock illustration in the emotional layer, measured rather than judged. Pixels with saturation > 0.45 and value > 0.35: exactly zero in 01_pulse, 02_chat, 03_us, 05_settings, 10_first_run, 12_search and 17_setup_pwa; 0.658 per cent in 04_moments and 0.053 per cent in 14_media_viewer, both of which are the photograph and video content itself; 0.087 per cent in 13_messenger_states, whose saturated pixels sit in one band at y 1755-1851, x 293-960 with mean RGB 177/76/69 - the red 'it would not go / send it again' failure ink. The emotional vocabulary is 36 named feelings (crops/haptics_strip.png) carried by physical objects: a shallow bowl for 'here', a soft cloth for 'breathe', a plaster for 'it's okay', a stone for 'steady', a mug for 'i'll make you tea', a twisted sweet wrapper for 'nyeh', cut-paper confetti, a folded cone for 'paper hat', a paper bunting for 'yes'. surfaces.json measures 62 object surfaces, names 34 of the 36 feelings as having a measured or read surface, records 4 more as pen marks the app draws, and leaves named_but_neither empty. Every object is lit and casts a shadow onto the sheet or desk it lands on.

The voice holds in every string I could read off the artifacts. 'write something', "first one's yours.", 'nothing to do. suspicious.', "nowhere planned. that's fine.", 'put it back', 'let it interrupt you', 'read the six words off the other phone', 'nothing from them since you last looked', 'it would not go' / 'send it again'. No exclamation mark appears in any recorded displayed string - the three '!' hits across all of evidence are strings.json's own pattern and two Dart null-assertion operators (next!, durationMs!). The reader is never called a user and the app never names itself on any screen; pwa.json's manifest name is 'the other phone', which is the one place a product name would conventionally sit.

None of the three tells the fourth anti-goal names is present. Tiling: 2-D autocorrelation over a 1200x1500 desk patch in 10_first_run and over paper in 17_setup_pwa finds no local maximum beyond lag 20 with prominence above 0.01 in either axis - the lag(8,0)=0.94 correlation is monotonic decay along the grain, not a period - and tears.json records 8 notes on 02_chat drawing 8 distinct tears from a pool of 56 with zero repeats. Procedural noise overlay: lag-1 autocorrelation of the Gaussian-sigma-3 high-pass residual is 0.97/0.77 on blank paper, 0.78/0.84 in a torn note interior, 0.70/0.93 on a module card and 0.80/0.83 on the desk, where per-pixel procedural noise would sit near zero; and no overlay rides on image content, the residual inside 14_media_viewer's photograph measuring 0.686 grey levels against paper's 3.5-31.7. Beige rounded rectangle: the flattest surfaces in the build are near-white (mean luma 218-240), square-cornered, and show fibre under a contrast stretch.

The 300 per cent crops earn the concept. In crops/02_chat_300_edge.png and crops/02_chat_300_hand.png the sheet ends in a true deckle with individual fibres standing off it and a contact shadow that follows the tear's contour; hand.json puts 58 of 500 ink marks within 0.85 IoU of a twin (11.6 per cent, falling to 0.4 per cent at 0.95 and 0 at 0.99), which is a hand repeating itself a little rather than a font repeating itself exactly.
verdict: None of the four forbidden interpretations appears in this build, and on the three that can be settled by measurement the evidence is unambiguous: zero saturated pixels in seven of ten stills with every exception traced to photograph content or one band of red failure ink, no badge or count or streak warning on any surface including a rituals module carrying 53 kept events, no exclamation mark or marketing phrase in any recorded displayed string, no tile period in desk or paper, and a high-pass residual whose lag-1 autocorrelation of 0.70-0.97 rules out the procedural noise overlay outright. The riskiest anti-goal is the one that holds best: at 300 per cent the paper ends in real fibre, 54 paper stocks and 56 tear masks are in play with no repeat on screen, and the feeling vocabulary is 36 physically-modelled objects rather than glyphs. What keeps this off full marks is one measurable thinning and three limits on how far the sweep reaches. The thinning is the module glance cards on 03_us: machine-straight to 0.84 px of column std over 155 rows, flattest window 1.47 against the harness's own 4.58 for real paper, sitting between torn rows that measure 26-51, with a 15 px cast shadow on the wood beside them - not the beige rounded rectangle the anti-goal names, since they are near-white, square-cornered and still fibrous under a stretch, but the weakest material in the build and pointed the wrong way. The limits are that flat.json reports ok:false on four stills where I reproduce its numbers but disagree with three of its four verdicts on inspection (05_settings and both 17_setup_pwa windows are low-amplitude but genuine texture inside torn sheets, and 14_media_viewer's window is the sky of the photograph being viewed, not paper at all, which is the check measuring image content); that grain.json declares a 3.6 threshold, measures 5.13 and 5.49 against it, and still says ok; and above all that the voice sweep rests on 116 of 3672 literals while both Android artifacts are absent, so the whole Android surface is uninspected for all four anti-goals. That absence is a reason and not an excuse - the machine has no /dev/kvm, adbd took 113 minutes to answer with no framework behind it, and nothing was faked from the PWA - but a row that certifies a build against four prohibitions cannot claim to have checked a surface it never saw. The row meets its floor and no finding is blocking.
not_worth_opening: evidence/logs/11_chat_scroll.fling.json and evidence/logs/scroll_webkit.json - per-frame scroll displacement and WebKit build/raster cost. Neither can show a badge, an emoji, a marketing string or a paper surface; they belong to the motion and performance rows, not to this one.

evidence/logs/haptics.json - the 23 KB raw vibration patterns. I read haptics.check.json and crops/haptics_strip.png instead, which give me what this row needs: all 36 feeling names, their registers, and that no two patterns are closer than 26.49 felt distance against an 18.0 floor. The raw amplitude arrays add nothing a reader can see or read.
